_README: TEMPLATE, not a drop-in. Merge the parts you want into your own
~/.claude/settings.json; do not copy this file over yours.
Replace <PYTHON_EXE> with an absolute path to a Python 3.10+ interpreter and
<CLAUDE_HOME> with the absolute path to your .claude directory. Claude Code
does not expand ~ or environment variables inside a hook command, which is
why these are absolute and why they are the only machine-bound values here.
The permissions block is ONE operator's threat model, published as a worked
example. Read every line before adopting it; an allowlist you did not decide
on is worse than no allowlist. The `ask` entries are the important half —
they make the config edit itself a confirmed action.
env.CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW widens the auto-compact trigger to 400k
tokens. The compact-recovery mechanism's bands (context_runway_shadow.py:
150k/300k) and its own docstrings are calibrated assuming this window; drop
the key (or lower it) and the notices simply fire earlier relative to the
platform default, nothing breaks.
OMISSIONS, named rather than left pointing at files you do not have (all
declared in tools/share-manifest.toml with a reason):
· the two external-dispatch hooks — they gate a dispatcher this share
does not ship;
· session_board_register.py and project_registry_gist.py — each is one
half of a source-environment tool (the session board, the project
registry) that does not ship; the rule they serve degrades to the
by-hand steps stated in claude-ops/ops/20-dispatch.md §7a;
· secret_file_guard.py — a local secrets policy, not a portable rule;
· xi_card_guard.py — a shadow probe for a cross-index pipeline this
share does not carry (registry.json names real absolute store roots,
its parser lives in tools/cross-index/); telemetry/ is excluded too;
· intake_guard.py and intake_match_shadow.py — the DENY guard and the
shadow match probe for the lesson-intake store (ops/lessons/); both
are one half of tools/closeout-intake/ (the CLI that alone can write
that store), which this share does not carry. intake_guard.py's own
deny message points at that CLI, so shipping the guard without it
would block writes to a path this repo does not even ship (ops/lessons/
itself is excluded — only the generated ops/lessons.md index ships).
No by-hand fallback is named here; author your own lesson-record
convention if you want one.
· unattended_run.py (three mounts: PreToolUse scope guard, UserPromptSubmit
kickoff, Stop) — the whole [unattended-run] carrier is built on
tools/process-ledger/ (ledger.py, report.py), which this share does not
carry: the Stop guard's own block condition requires a report file only
that tool can generate, so shipping the hook without it would block
every session end once a run is kicked off. No fallback named; the
obligations text (scope discipline, a canary pair, a stop report) is a
pattern to re-implement against your own process-tracking tool, not a
file to copy.
· the SessionEnd memory-pipeline mount — its script now ships as
compact-recovery/preserve.py, but the mount still points outside
hooks/ and this template mounts hooks/ and nothing else; the optional
SessionEnd block lives in compact-recovery/README.md.
· hooks/fieldwork_threshold_notice.py — RETIRED at the source 2026-09-11
(user ruling R-3, rules-debt audit): unregistered from settings.json
after 293 shadow rows measured >=52% quantifiably false. The file and
its telemetry shape are kept here for provenance/rollback (the source
kept them too), but no mount exists to carry over — this template
mirrors that.
Every hook in hooks/ that is MOUNTED AT THE SOURCE is mounted here — if you
find one that is not, that is a defect in this template, not a
recommendation. Three .py files directly under hooks/ are deliberately NOT
mounted, none is a defect: hooks/deny_receipt.py and hooks/handoff_snapshot.py
are plain shared libraries (deny/notice receipt clauses; snapshot_path,
is_fresh, notice) imported by other hooks — each has no event to mount at,
the same way a Python module you import is not itself wired into an event;
hooks/fieldwork_threshold_notice.py is the retired probe named above. The
four files under hooks/tests/ (test_browser_pane_scope_guard.py,
test_fieldwork_threshold_notice.py, test_instructions_loaded_logger.py,
test_transcript_read_guard.py) are regression matrices, run by hand
(`python hooks/tests/<name>.py`), not hooks — mounting a test as a hook
would put a test harness on every matched tool call.
Verify after wiring: run each hook by hand with empty stdin and check it
exits 0 (they are all fail-open), then confirm the matcher fires on a real
call. A hook registered at a path that does not exist makes python exit 2,
which Claude Code treats as a blocking error for every matched tool call.
